page_note: This page has no cosmological substrate teaching. The first half is hortatory instruction to brothers/members about how to eat and not eat in luxury (with the Living Cross referenced in a ritual-pastoral context, not a cosmological-mapping context). Then a closing dialogue exchange between Apostle and disciple, then chapter heading 96 "The Chapter of the Man who asks: For what reason am I habitually still at certain times, while disturbed at other times?" — a psychological/anthropological question rather than a cosmological one — followed by the disciple's self-description. Teaching purity 0.000 confirms reading: this is entirely editorial/hortatory/dialogue framing. Strong seam at seg 13 (ⲧⲟⲧⲉ ⲡⲁⲭⲉ ⲡⲁⲡⲟⲥⲧⲟⲗⲟⲥ).

segments.temporal_note: Pastoral antithesis: 'pain for an hour, rest unto eternity' — exhortative register addressed to audience.
Continuation: 'shall it become for her among the holy ones' — pastoral promise.
'But this is what I enjoin' — explicit speaker-to-audience injunction frame.
Vocative 'my brothers and my members' + prohibition 'do not!' — paradigmatic hortatory.

Living Cross (ⲡⲓⲥⲧⲁⲩⲣⲟⲥ ⲉⲧⲁⲛϩ) appears here not as cosmological mapping but as the object of ritual conduct — 'do not let his hand release and turn the Living Cross to luxury.' Pastoral-ritual register.
'rather, be path-setters' — direct exhortation.
'in the speech to the catechumens' — explicit ecclesial category (ⲛⲕⲁⲧⲏⲭⲟⲩⲙⲉⲛⲟⲥ). Score flags ecclesial=71.43.
'we proclaim it that you may proclaim it' — first-person plural pastoral mission.
Continued instruction on how to eat — 'when you draw near to eat her, do not...'
Continued prohibition: 'eat her in luxury, tippling, carousing.'
'rather, eat her in great hunger' — antithetical exhortation.
'drink her in great thirst, bear care of your body' — ascetic instruction.
'by means of her' — close of exhortation unit.
SEAM flagged. 'Then said the Apostle to that disciple' — pure dialogue frame attribution.
Continuation of Apostle's address to disciple: 'Behold, you have heard what I have proclaimed to you.'
'concerning the desire — you alone are without sin therein' — Apostle's pronouncement to disciple.
Disciple-response narrative: 'When that disciple heard, he was persuaded, rejoiced, was raised up.'
'said to him: I give thanks to thee, my Lord' — disciple's thanksgiving formula.
Continuation of thanksgiving: 'thou givest rest to our heart.'
'in gentleness; from now forth, in the words also' — closing of disciple's speech.
'living, we shall live unto thee in thy living words' — disciple's hagiographic praise.
'which we have heard from thee' — close of dialogue exchange.
Chapter number '96' — editorial structural numbering.
'The Chapter of the Man' — Kephalaia chapter heading formula (editorial).

'who asks: For what reason am I habitually' — chapter heading framing the question. The question is psychological/anthropological (rest vs. disturbance), not a cosmological-correspondential mapping question.
'still at certain times, while disturbed' — continuation of chapter heading question.
'at other times?' — close of chapter heading.
'Again, said a disciple to the Illuminator (ⲡⲓⲙⲫⲱⲥⲧⲏⲣ): I beseech thee' — paradigmatic dialogue frame opener.
'my Lord, that thou make known to me concerning this matter' — pure beseeching formula, no substantive cosmological content.
Disciple describing his own psychological states: 'There are times that I am still in my heart, my reflection...' — anthropological question, not cosmological mapping.
'all my teachings are established in their place, I conduct myself' — disciple's self-description.
'my works, I proclaim my words to every man' — continued self-description of disciple's good state.
'I am at peace of heart in the joy of the Mind (ⲡⲛⲟⲩⲥ)' — disciple's account of his rest. Nous appears but as predicate of disciple's psychological state, not as a cosmic-mapping subject.
